answer.question: For the 'patients who rated the hospital 9 or 10' survey measure, do any Texas hospitals have scores from more than one reporting period (so a change from the prior period could be computed)? answer.answer: Yes, the results show 297 Texas hospitals with a score. The largest number of reporting periods for any one hospital is 1, and 0 hospitals have more than one period, so none have scores from multiple periods to compare.
answer.sql: SELECT UPPER(m.measure_id) AS measure_id, m.measure_name, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospitals_with_score, MAX(p.reporting_periods) AS max_reporting_periods_per_hospital, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE p.reporting_periods > 1) AS hospitals_with_multiple_periods FROM (SELECT mv.facility_id, COUNT(DISTINCT (mv.period_start, mv.period_end)) AS reporting_periods FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') AND h.state = 'TX' AND mv.score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY mv.facility_id) AS p CROSS JOIN hq.measures AS m WHERE UPPER(m.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') GROUP BY m.measure_id, m.measure_name LIMIT 200

answer.sql: WITH tx AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, UPPER(measure_id) AS measure_id, score FROM hq.v_tx_latest WHERE UPPER(measure_id) IN ('READM_30_PN', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'SEP_1') AND score IS NOT NULL), measure_stats AS (SELECT measure_id, AVG(score) AS mean_score, STDDEV(score) AS sample_sd FROM tx GROUP BY measure_id), standardized AS (SELECT t.facility_id, t.facility_name, t.county, t.measure_id, CASE WHEN t.measure_id = 'READM_30_PN' THEN -((t.score - s.mean_score) / NULLIF(s.sample_sd, 0)) ELSE (t.score - s.mean_score) / NULLIF(s.sample_sd, 0) END AS z_score FROM tx AS t JOIN measure_stats AS s ON s.measure_id = t.measure_id), composites AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, AVG(z_score) AS composite FROM standardized GROUP BY facility_id, facility_name, county HAVING COUNT(*) = 3), ranked AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, composite, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY composite DESC, facility_name, county) AS top_rank, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY composite ASC, facility_name, county) AS bottom_rank FROM composites), selected AS (SELECT 1 AS group_order, 'Top' AS group_name, top_rank AS group_rank, facility_name, county, composite FROM ranked WHERE top_rank <= 10 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS group_order, 'Bottom' AS group_name, bottom_rank AS group_rank, facility_name, county, composite FROM ranked WHERE bottom_rank <= 10) SELECT group_name, group_rank, facility_name, county, ROUND(CAST(composite AS DECIMAL), 2) AS composite_z_score FROM selected ORDER BY group_order, group_rank LIMIT 200

records.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.

answer.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.
answer.answer: Among the six measures, Texas hospitals’ shares above or below the national average, as appropriate for the measure, are: HAI_1_SIR — national average 0.58; 151 Texas hospitals with a score, 99 beat the average (65.6%). MORT_30_HF — 11.07; 206 with a score, 132 beat it (64.1%). SEP_1 — 63.79; 233 with a score, 146 beat it (62.7%). READM_30_PN — 17.34; 258 with a score, 150 beat it (58.1%). H_RECMND_DY — 71.22; 297 with a score, 158 beat it (53.2%). H_STAR_RATING — 3.27; 229 with a score, 92 beat it (40.2%).
answer.sql: WITH selected_measures AS (SELECT m.measure_id, m.measure_name, m.higher_is_better FROM hq.measures AS m WHERE m.measure_id IN ('READM_30_PN', 'MORT_30_HF', 'HAI_1_SIR', 'SEP_1', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'H_STAR_RATING')), scored_periods AS (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.period_start DESC NULLS LAST) AS period_rank FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN selected_measures AS sm ON sm.measure_id = mv.measure_id WHERE mv.score IS NOT NULL), latest_scores AS (SELECT sp.facility_id, sp.measure_id, sp.score FROM scored_periods AS sp WHERE sp.period_rank = 1), national AS (SELECT ls.measure_id, AVG(ls.score) AS national_average, sm.higher_is_better FROM latest_scores AS ls JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = ls.facility_id JOIN selected_measures AS sm ON sm.measure_id = ls.measure_id GROUP BY ls.measure_id, sm.higher_is_better), texas AS (SELECT ls.measure_id, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospitals_with_score, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE (n.higher_is_better AND ls.score > n.national_average) OR (NOT n.higher_is_better AND ls.score < n.national_average)) AS texas_hospitals_beating_average FROM latest_scores AS ls JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = ls.facility_id JOIN national AS n ON n.measure_id = ls.measure_id WHERE h.state = 'TX' GROUP BY ls.measure_id) SELECT sm.measure_id, sm.measure_name, ROUND(CAST(n.national_average AS DECIMAL), 2) AS national_average, t.texas_hospitals_with_score, t.texas_hospitals_beating_average, ROUND(100.0 * t.texas_hospitals_beating_average / NULLIF(t.texas_hospitals_with_score, 0), 1) AS share_beating_national_pct FROM selected_measures AS sm JOIN national AS n ON n.measure_id = sm.measure_id JOIN texas AS t ON t.measure_id = sm.measure_id ORDER BY share_beating_national_pct DESC, sm.measure_id LIMIT 200
